recipes.name: Spicy Beef Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes with juice
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle dark beer
4 fresh hot chile peppers, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook onions, garlic, ground beef and cubed sirloin in oil for 10 minutes, or until the meat is well browned and the onions are tender.

Mix in the diced tomatoes with juice, dark beer, coffee, tomato paste and beef broth. Season with brown sugar, chili powder, cumin, cocoa powder, oregano, cayenne pepper, coriander and salt. Stir in 2 cans of the beans and hot chile peppers. Reduce heat to low, and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Stir in the 2 remaining cans of beans, and simmer for another 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Beef Chili
raw_recipe.description: Here's a spicy chili recipe you'll love, combining ground beef and cubed top sirloin. Other ingredients include beer, strong-brewed coffee, unsweetened cocoa powder and ground cumin.

video.description: This video shows you how to make a thick, spicy chili flavored with dark beer, strong-brewed coffee, and chopped fresh chile peppers. It has two types of beef, too: ground beef and sirloin. As it slowly simmers, it develops deep, spicy flavors that just won’t quit.

review.reviewBody: As a side note, I always chuckle when people rate a recipe without first trying it "as-written" and then say it isn't good. With this recipe in particular, following the instructions at least once is lesson in learning you won't regret. We were very impressed with this chili. We did make it as written, the only variable being the "dark beer" we selected (since the recipe doesn't specify a brand). We chose not to use Guiness and used a locally brewed dark that's a bit less sweet since previous reviews had suggested that the recipe had too much sugar. I'd have to agree. Next time we make it (and it was good enough that there will be a next time!), we'll cut back on cocoa and just a bit on the sugar, as other reviewers suggested. That said, as-is, it's an excellent recipe. I strongly encourage you to make it exactly as written first, so you know what adjustments you need to suit your taste--it's not "too" anything--it has a nice mix of sweet and spice and it's hard to say how much you'll need to adjust to suit your taste. The balance of flavors is really quite impressive. In other regards, the texture, consistency, and ratio of meat & beans is just right.

This is a very interesting recipe. As with all chili recipes, modifications can be made for personal taste. I used all stew beef for mine and made it in the crock pot. Only 1 onion, which I cooked while I browned the meat, and then a can of kidney beans and a can of black beans (not 4 cans of beans). The beans do need to be drained. There's a lot of liquid there. I cut the brown sugar to 1/4 cup and used a nice Porter for the beer. I also just used a large can of diced green chilies and only 1/2 tsp of cayenne and 2 Tbsp of chili powder. We found the spice just fine that way. Oddly, the flavors mesh. Yes, it's sweet, but not in a bad way just a surprising way.

I’ve made this chili many times now and started out exactly as directed and it is absolutely wonderfully delicious! I now change things up almost every time but what stays constant is the seasoning and liquids, except salt… definitely not enough salt. I brown the sirloin first to get a nice fond then ground beef, onions and garlic. I’ve done half beans, no beans, half beans with veggies (mushrooms, peppers, sweet potatoes, corn etc. ) veggies and no meat😲. The point is that it’s chili so do whatever but the seasoning and liquids can’t be beat.

When making chili you MUST cook it, let it cool for a day, and re-heat. If you don't, you're going to get an inferior dish. A lot of people forget this. This is a great recipe and If you follow it you will make great chili every time. I reduced the amount of chili peppers, the recipe calls for 4.. that's very spicy. I used 2 and it had a nice kick to it. I thought it called for more salt, but that's a very subjective thing.

This is very close to a chili recipe that was published many years ago in the Dallas Morning News. A couple of things I'd change. The skin on the kidney beans doesn't soften enough when added at Step 3, so instead add ALL beans at Step 2. Also, the amount of brown sugar is way too much and ruins an otherwise good recipe. Replace the brown sugar with molasses instead. Finally, the chili peppers. Add one chili pepper to start with, then if needed, add more one at a time until you've reached your desired heat level.

This is my all-time favorite chili recipe, and I get compliments every time I make it. Something about the richness of the cocoa, beer and coffee plus a little sweetness just really works so well here. I usually use extra meat, about 1.5lb ground beef and 1.5lb sirloin that I cut into cubes myself. I try to sauté the beef and onions for a little while to tenderize the beef cubes. I also use 2-3 jalapeños instead of the other peppers due to convenience. I will add more or less cayenne based on the spiciness of the jalapeños. Love this recipe and make this chili several times per year!

The coffee simply overpowered everything. In order to fix it, I added the following: 4 oz. green chiles, 1 tsp. ground chipotle, 1/2 tsp. garlic powder, 1 tsp. Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp. ground cumin, and 1 Tablespoon Cholula hot sauce (replacing 1/2 tsp. of the cayenne. The amount of brown sugar made it too sweet. I think 1/2 tsp. molasses would be an improvement. The additions helped to correct the problems of (1) lack of cumin made it not even taste like chili (2) overwhelming coffee flavor. I will be looking for a new recipe next time.

Really good!!! I did make a few modifications based on what I had though. I used a can of Yuengling for the beer and 2 jalapeños for the peppers. I did drain the meat before adding the spices and everything and only used one big can of chili beans instead of the 4 cans because I'm not a big bean fan. And followed some suggestions to only use 1/4 cup sugar but think a little more might be better next time. - it wasn't quite sweet enough the next day. I also used a tablespoon of espresso powder because I didn't have coffee. My husband said it was better than his chili ;) Will definitely make again!
ON a side note I also cook mine in a slow cooker for at least 4 hours if not a little more.

This was my first time cooking chili and it came out great. I made it as written except for the 4 chili peppers, I used 1 jalapeño instead- I have some family members who won’t eat anything spicy hot. I used Sam Adams Boston Lager for the beer. This chili was nice and thick, with a good balance of sweet and spicy flavor, and no mouth burning heat. The sirloin chunks were a nice addition- my husband immediately picked up on the fact this wasn’t just a usual all ground beef chili and remarked “that’s why this so good”. I like that this has more flavor than many tomato tasting chili’s, and I like the sweetness- it sets this chili apart. I will definitely make this again.

Fantastic recipe. I've made this a lot, and it's one of my favorites. The first time I followed the recipe pretty much to the letter. Afterwards, I've enjoyed making a vegetarian version using button mushrooms chopped fine instead of ground beef, and thick cut portobellos instead of sirloin. I also sub 2 cans of black beans instead of all 4 kidney beans, which gives it a nice SW flavor. I like to use some home-made cold brew for the coffee, as it has a nice, smooth, sweet, low-acidity flavor compared to hot brewed coffee. Great recipe, one of our favorites!
I have been using this exact recipe for years and it is definitely a keeper. I don't use the sirloin, just replace with additional ground beef!
I loved it, but it was a little spicy for some people.
I thought it was way too sweet. If I were to make it again, I would cut the sugar in half

I've been making this recipe for years and everyone absolutely LOVES it. The ONLY tweek I make is I use less than half of the brown sugar. Maybe only 1 tablespoon. It turns out great every time and there's never leftovers.

I made this chili in my instapot after cooking the meat and did cut down the brown sugar to a 1/4 cup. I still found it to be a little sweet however I did not have the cumin seeds and did not add the fresh chili peppers as I have an aversion to things that are too spicy. I do like this and added white pepper for more spice. I also added bell peppers. It turned out very well and I am sure will only improve on the next day. When I make again I will try with some chili peppers. Thank you for sharing.

I have been making this recipe for years now. I have won 1st place in 2 different Chili tasting contest with this recipe. I have made only 2 changes to it over the years. I only use 1/4 cup of Brown Sugar as I thought it was a little too sweet with 1/2 cup. And I use 2 cans of beans, drained, not 4. I do put them in at the beginning of the cook time. Other than that I make it as it is written. I have always received many compliments. I have passed this recipe down to my kids and family. This will always be my go to recipe.
Perfect balance of heat and sweet. Recipe always requested by guests. Definitely in our list of top favorite recipes.

First make I followed the recipe exactly. It's a tad sweet but wow, the flavor is really packed in here. This is a luxurious chili with a low bean ratio IMO. If making as a budget-friendly meal you could easily double the beans. I will make again with dry/soaked beans instead of canned. The instructions did not specify whether to rinse the beans or not, two cans went in with the goo, two cans got rinsed. I think rinsing two of them was a good idea as the goo can impart a slimy texture. This recipe was not slimy at all. I won my office chili cook-off this week with this recipe. Searing the meat is very important. Another quick tip, cook on low for an hour, refrigerate, and finish the cook the next day. Great recipe.

I have several chili recipes. But for me and my personal tastes this is my hands down favorite. Not the favorite of everyone but all at least like it. So love the savory sweet and the two contrasting beef textures. The ingredients do make a difference but once I forgot the beer, once the coffee and another time just lite beer. But it’s always super tasty to this experienced home chef. Give it a try. Serve it next day, even better, over a bit of pasta. Yum! Bon Appetite!
